entry.title: Differences Between foldl and foldr in Haskell
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | blog.haskell.org | discussion

Haskell's `foldl` and `foldr` functions differ in associativity despite both traversing lists from left to right. While both traverse lists from the left, `foldl` is left-associative and `foldr` is right-associative, which fundamentally changes their behavior in lazy evaluation environments.

In lazy evaluation, `foldl` can lead to linear space complexity by building large, nested thunks, whereas the strict version `foldl'` is recommended for constant-space accumulation. In contrast, `foldr` can facilitate streaming and allow for processing infinite lists when the combining function is lazy in its second argument.

entry.title: FunSQL Explains Data-Oriented vs. Syntax-Oriented SQL Query Builders
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | mechanicalrabbit.github.io | discussion

The article distinguishes between two types of SQL query builders: data-oriented and syntax-oriented. Data-oriented builders—such as FunSQL, EF/LINQ, and dbplyr—treat pipeline nodes as sequential data processing steps, meaning the order of operations directly determines the query's output. Conversely, syntax-oriented builders—such as Active Record and Laravel—treat nodes as components for constructing a SQL syntax tree, making the order of assembly irrelevant to the final query.

Syntax-oriented builders are easier to implement but inherit the rigid clause order and grammatical limitations of SQL. Data-oriented builders attempt to represent complex data transformations through query nesting and SQL pushdown, though they may struggle to support the full breadth of SQL's specialized features. FunSQL is designed specifically to expose the complete expressive power of SQL, including recursive queries and lateral joins, by focusing on data processing semantics rather than syntax-driven construction.

The Aho-Corasick algorithm enables simultaneous multi-pattern matching within a sequence by constructing a finite state automaton from a trie. It utilizes suffix links to navigate the automaton upon transition failure and output links to identify overlapping pattern matches.

entry.title: Intel 8087 Tangent Algorithm Implementation Details
entry.content:

The 8087 floating-point coprocessor uses a hybrid algorithm to compute the tangent function (FPTAN) with high speed and 64-bit accuracy. The approach combines the CORDIC algorithm for initial angle reduction with a Padé approximant—a rational polynomial—to compute the remaining small angle.

Through microscopic analysis of the chip's circuitry and microcode ROM, the process was identified as a three-stage sequence: pseudo-division to generate CORDIC decision bits, calculating a rational approximation, and pseudo-multiplication to perform rotations. This specific implementation avoids slow division operations, enabling significantly faster computation than the 8086 microprocessor.

entry.title: First Principles Thinking in the Era of Agentic AI Development
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | sunilsadasivan.com | hacker news

The article argues that senior engineers risk a period of stagnation—referred to as a "death spiral"—when accumulated experience prevents them from approaching new technical paradigms with a fresh perspective. To counter this, the author advocates for first principles thinking, which involves deconstructing complex problems into their most fundamental truths rather than relying on analogies or historical technical constraints.

This mental framework is presented as essential for navigating the shift toward agentic AI development. By setting aside existing biases and focusing on small, rapid learning loops, engineers can maintain momentum and effectively integrate AI agents into their development workflows.

Cybersecurity firm UpGuard has identified approximately 16,000 Supabase databases that are publicly exposing sensitive user information, including names, addresses, phone numbers, and passwords. These exposures are primarily attributed to user misconfigurations, often stemming from improper security settings or vulnerabilities in code generated by AI tools.

The identified datasets contain a wide variety of sensitive data, ranging from contact information for immigration services to license plates and data from an African consulate. While Supabase maintains that security is a shared responsibility between the platform and its customers, the findings highlight growing risks associated with the rise of "vibe-coded" applications built with AI assistance.
